entries.title: Pathways: Surveys — see what members want and manage quick questions
entries.summary: A new **Surveys** section in the Pathways admin lets super users view member answer insights and manage one-tap questions. The **What members are telling us** tab shows KPIs, answer breakdowns by choice with weekly sparklines, and "more of / less of" themes derived from profile signals, with period and cohort filters and **Export answers (CSV)**. The **Questions** tab lets you write questions yourself or use **Ask the guide to draft questions** — drafts land as *Waiting for your OK* and can be approved or discarded. Live questions can be paused or archived; paused ones resumed; archived ones restored. All questions support search, status/author/location filters, column sort, and **Export CSV**.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Pathways; then Pathways → Surveys

entries.use_case: Organizations running Pathways can now see exactly what members want more or less of — and ask targeted follow-up questions — without building a separate survey tool. The guide-drafted questions feature is especially useful when you are not sure what to ask: describe your learning goal and the guide proposes ready-to-approve questions.

cs_action.note: Feature is behind a flag and restricted to super users only. Confirm the flag is enabled for the org before walking a customer through it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Pathways customer asks how to understand member preferences or wants to collect lightweight feedback without a formal survey.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs already on Pathways beta who want member-preference data to inform content decisions.
internal.gotchas: Members never see the word 'survey' — they see one-tap 'quick questions'. The Surveys page is super-user-only behind a feature flag; regular org admins do not see it until the flag is on.
internal.talk_track: Pathways now tells you what your members want more of and less of, straight from the quick questions they answer in the app. You can write your own questions or let the guide draft them from a plain-language goal — then approve or discard each draft before it goes live.

draft.docs_gap: The /pathways/overview guide should add a Surveys section covering the What members are telling us insights tab, the Questions tab (including guide-drafted questions and the Waiting for your OK workflow), question lifecycle actions (approve, discard, pause, resume, archive, restore), and CSV export for both tabs.
draft.why_use_it: Pathways Surveys surfaces what members are telling you through one-tap questions embedded in their experience. Instead of long post-event surveys, members answer in the moment, and the admin aggregates those signals into themes, choice breakdowns and weekly trends so you can adjust your program content and format in real time. The guide-drafted questions feature helps you ask the right things by turning a plain-language goal into ready-to-review questions, complete with the guide's rationale for each one.

entries.title: Pathways members can connect their own AI assistant
entries.summary: Pathways members can now attach a personal AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and others) to their Pathways record via **Connect your assistant**. Two connection methods are available: a connector link with a one-time code (OAuth 2.1 / PKCE) or a personal key shown once for assistants that accept a URL and key. Members choose exactly which data the assistant may read or act on — **My picks**, **My plan and schedule**, **My learning**, and **My profile** — and which actions it may take, such as **Save or dismiss picks**, **Add sessions to my plan**, and **Ask questions**. Permissions can be changed at any time, and every successful assistant call is logged in plain language. Members can disconnect one assistant or all at once.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the Pathways assistant feature; then Pathways App → Profile → Connect your assistant

where.path: Pathways App → Profile → Connect your assistant

entries.use_case: Members who use AI assistants daily can give their assistant direct, scoped access to their Pathways record — letting it read their plan, save picks, and answer questions on their behalf — without sharing their login credentials or granting broader access than they choose.

cs_action.note: Feature is behind the existing Pathways super-user/app flag; CS must confirm the flag is on for the org before members can see Connect your assistant.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Pathways customer asks about AI assistant integration or wants members to interact with their plan through Claude, ChatGPT, or similar tools.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs already on the Pathways beta whose members are active AI assistant users.
internal.staff_path: Pathways App → Profile → Connect your assistant
internal.gotchas: Personal key tokens are shown only once at creation; if a member loses it they must generate a new one. Assistant tokens (sbpw_ prefix) are scoped only to /me routes and can never manage other assistants. Tokens expire after 90 days and must be reconnected.
internal.talk_track: Members can attach Claude or ChatGPT directly to their Pathways record and choose exactly what the assistant can see and do — picks, plan, learning, profile — with a full activity log and one-click disconnect.

draft.docs_gap: The /agents/overview guide should add a dedicated section explaining how Pathways members (not organizers) connect their own assistant, covering both the OAuth connector-link flow and the personal-key flow, scope choices, the activity log, and how to disconnect.
draft.why_use_it: Pathways lets members carry their learning and session engagement across every event in an organization. Connecting a personal AI assistant extends that continuity into the tools members already use: the assistant can read their picks and plan, add sessions, and answer questions, all within the scopes the member explicitly grants. Tokens are hashed and expire after 90 days, and every action the assistant takes is logged so members always know what happened on their behalf.

entries.title: Pathways admin: approval state and SSO sign-in options now reflect actual behaviour
entries.summary: In the Pathways admin, the **Approvals** page now shows approved records as "not sent yet — sending turns on when Pathways launches," so staff can see that approving records the decision without triggering any member communication. On the **Settings → Sign-in** page, the **SAML** and **OpenID Connect** options remain visible but are disabled with the note "We connect this with you. Ask your Sessionboard contact," preventing silent fallback to email-code sign-in when SSO is not yet configured.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Pathways; then Pathways → Settings

entries.use_case: Staff approving Pathways members can now trust that "approved" means the decision is recorded — not that a message has gone out — so they won't mistakenly assume members have been notified before Pathways launches. The disabled SSO options prevent confusion about why members receive email codes instead of their expected single sign-on.

cs_action.note: Pathways is behind useSuperUser(); confirm with the account team before discussing with customers. SSO (SAML/OIDC) for Pathways must be connected by Sessionboard staff — the UI now makes this clear.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Pathways beta asks why approved members haven't received anything, or why members are getting email codes instead of SSO.
internal.gotchas: SAML and OIDC options are visible but disabled for all orgs until Sessionboard staff complete the SSO connection. An org already configured for one of them will still see it selected.
internal.talk_track: Approving a member in Pathways records your decision; the actual send happens automatically when Pathways goes live. If you want SSO for member sign-in, reach out and we'll set it up with you.

draft.docs_gap: The Pathways overview guide should document the approvals lifecycle (decision recorded vs. sent) and explain that SAML/OIDC sign-in requires Sessionboard to complete the connection.
draft.why_use_it: Pathways lets you manage member approvals and sign-in settings for your organisation's pathway programme. The approvals workflow records decisions ahead of launch so your team can work through the queue without triggering premature communications. Sign-in settings let you choose how members authenticate once the programme is live.

entries.title: Pathways Ask answers members' own credit, renewal, due and plan questions directly
entries.summary: In the Pathways member app, **Ask** now answers personal questions — "How many credits do I still need?", "When does my membership renew?", "What's due?", "What's my plan?" — with exact figures from the member's own record (e.g. "You need 6 more credits by December 31. You have 18 of 24.") instead of returning generic course titles. Courses the member has already completed are also excluded from program search suggestions.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Pathways; then the member app's Ask feature

entries.use_case: Members who ask Ask "How many credits do I still need?" or "When does my membership renew?" now get a precise, personalised answer drawn from their own record — not a list of course titles — so they can act immediately without hunting through their profile.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic for all orgs with the Pathways app flag enabled; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that Ask returns course titles instead of personal credit or renewal data, or when demoing the Pathways member app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organisations with the Pathways beta and the member app enabled.
internal.gotchas: Fix is behind the existing super-user/app flag; no schema changes. The response shape is unchanged so no downstream integrations are affected.
internal.talk_track: Ask in the member app now answers 'How many credits do I still need?' with the member's exact numbers and a Start action, and excludes courses they've already finished from suggestions.

draft.docs_gap: The Pathways overview guide should document what personal questions Ask can answer in the member app and how it draws from the member's own record.
draft.why_use_it: Pathways gives members a guided, personalised learning journey inside your event or membership programme. The built-in Ask assistant lets members ask questions in plain language and get answers about their progress, requirements and schedule without leaving the app. Use it to reduce support requests and keep members on track toward their credit or renewal goals.
